card.name: Linking words after necessity or only-way phrases
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as that, but, is, should or as that come right after phrases of need or sole means, like "necessary", "the only way", "natural and proper" or "demand". They appear in older, formal prose.

modes.label: That after need words
modes.description: The word that follows an adjective or verb of necessity or demand and opens a clause.

modes.label: After only way
modes.description: The word but or is follows a phrase like "the only way" or "no other way".
modes.example: There is no other way<< but>> to seek each group in its ownl

modes.label: Rhetorical should
modes.description: The word should follows why at the start of a rhetorical question.
